title: Which prefix? — the whole table, as practice

blocks.text: See below for a table the prefixes, their primary meanings, and the prepositions that accompany them, adapted from Muravyova.

head: prefix
primary meaning
prepositions
rows: Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы-
Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в-
из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.
Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у-
в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.
Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при-
в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.
Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под-
Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way
в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.
Movement across, through, or past something
сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition
Movement across, from one point to another; through
с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.
Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place
Movement involving the entire area concerned and carried out in all directions
Movement onto the surface of an object
Convergent movement from various directions towards one center. Antonym: раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)
Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся)
по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.
Beginning of unidirectional movement (with unidirectional verb of motion)
в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.; по + dat.
blocks.caption: Prefixed verbs of motion

exercises.why: **переезжаем** is the present tense (1st person plural) of **переезжать** (to move (to change residence); to cross, to run over, to drive over) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **переехать**. present: я переезжа́ю · ты переезжа́ешь · он переезжа́ет · мы переезжа́ем · вы переезжа́ете · они переезжа́ют. — Wiktionary, «переезжать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  Compare: «Завтра мы переедем в наш новый дом.» (future) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **выезжаем** (**выезжать**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **проезжаем** (**проезжать**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something; **уезжаем** (**уезжать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **отплывём** (**отплыть**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **приплывём** (**приплыть**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **проплывём** (**проплыть**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **приходите** is the present tense (2nd person plural) of **приходить** (to come (to), to arrive (at) (place, conclusion, state of abandonment, anger, insanity)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **прийти**. present: я прихожу́ · ты прихо́дишь · он прихо́дит · мы прихо́дим · вы прихо́дите · они прихо́дят. — Wiktionary, «приходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда? — Это старшина. Лейтенант в штабе? — Нет, он уже идёт (едет) сюда.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **обходите** (**обходить**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **переходите** (**переходить**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **подходите** (**подходить**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
